ambiguities.text: The specification does not define error response format when rate limit is exceeded
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard JSON-RPC error response with appropriate error code and message indicating rate limit exceeded.

ambiguities.text: The term 'trusted interfaces' is used without specifying what constitutes a trusted interface
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume trusted interfaces include localhost, private networks, and authenticated connections; untrusted includes public internet exposure.

ambiguities.text: The specification states clients 'MUST return up-to-date values reflecting most recent block header' but does not define acceptable staleness
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume configuration must reflect the current chain head with no more than one block lag.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes queried for configuration comparison are honest and return accurate data
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A network of colluding malicious nodes could mislead validators into accepting incorrect configurations.

implicit_assumptions.description: Client implementations correctly implement all configuration fields according to the specification
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inconsistent implementation could cause false positive mismatches or miss real configuration issues.

implicit_assumptions.description: Validators have access to known-good reference nodes for configuration comparison
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Isolated validators cannot verify their configuration against trusted sources.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot perform DNS/BGP hijacking to intercept eth_config queries to reference nodes
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Man-in-the-middle attacks could provide false configuration data to validators.
